description: This chart presents three pie charts labeled “easy,” “medium,” and “hard,” each depicting the distribution of four categories—N+K+, N−K+, N−K−, and N+K−—under a “Zero-Shot” evaluation. Each pie chart is divided into four colored segments: teal for N+K+, yellow for N−K+, orange for N−K−, and red for N+K−. The “easy” chart shows N+K+ at 55.4%, N−K+ at 38.3%, N−K− at 4.6%, and N+K− at 1.7%. The “medium” chart shows N+K+ at 58.8%, N−K+ at 35.4%, N−K− at 4.8%, and N+K− at 1.8%. The “hard” chart shows N+K+ at 37.3%, N−K+ at 37.9%, N−K− at 6.7%, and N+K− at 6.7%. The chart includes a legend on the right side matching the colors to their respective categories, and each slice is labeled with its percentage value. The slices are arranged in descending order within each pie chart, with the largest segment appearing at the top left.
